372915.title: Sup-norm conjecture for simultaneous eigenvectors of supersingular isogeny graphs
372915.statement:
Let $A_\ell$ denote the weighted adjacency matrix of the supersingular $\ell$-isogeny graph $\mathcal{G}(p,\ell)$ for all $\ell\neq p$. Let $v$ be an $L^2$-normalized simultaneous eigenvector of the operators $A_\ell$. **Sup-norm conjecture.** One has

$$
\|v\|_\infty \;\ll\; \frac{\log p}{\sqrt{p}}.
$$

This is evidence toward the strongest expected scale $p^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$ for sup-norms, which would express complete delocalization of eigenvectors. The stated logarithmic bound is presented as supporting evidence in the regular case $N=1$; the general optimal sup-norm bound is described as open.

372995.title: The graphical biclosed ornamentation lattice conjecture
372995.statement:
For a finite undirected graph $G$, let $\mathsf{B}$ be the **graphical pointed building set** of $G$, and let $\operatorname{Bicl}(\mathsf{B})$ denote the subposet of biclosed ornamentations in $\mathcal{O}(\mathsf{B})$. **Graphical biclosed ornamentation lattice conjecture.** The poset

$$
\operatorname{Bicl}(\mathsf{B})
$$

is a lattice. The claim is motivated by several natural examples in which this poset is a lattice, while the paper notes that it is not a lattice for arbitrary pointed building sets; whether the graphical case always has this property remains open.

Additional exhaustive pair tests for P6,C6,K1,5,K3,3 with 784,2125,4730,8214 ornamentations pass; see outputs/lattice6.json.

373098.title: Conjecture on the number of classes for curve orbits on a smooth Hermitian surface
373098.statement:
Let $X_I$ be the smooth Hermitian surface and let $C_{F_J}$ denote the curve associated with $F_J$. Set $O={\rm Aut}(X_I)C_{F_J}$, and let $d$ be the number of nontrivial classes in the associated relations $\{R_i\}_{i=0}^d$.

**Class-number conjecture.** If

$$
O={\rm Aut}(X_I)C_{F_J},
$$

then

$$
\nd=|\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_{q^2})|\quad\text{for all }q,
$$

that is, $(O,\{R_i\}_{i=0}^d)$ has $d=q^2+1$ classes.

The conjecture is motivated by the examples for $q=2$ and $q=3$, where the observed values of $d$ agree with $|\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_{q^2})|=q^2+1$. Its validity for all $q$ is left open in the source.

373150.title: The planar graph $(5m-1,m)$-choosability conjecture
373150.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let a graph be **$(a,b)$-choosable** if, for every assignment of lists of $a$ colors to its vertices, each list containing $a$ colors, one can choose a subset of $b$ colors from each list so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint subsets. The strong fractional choice number of a graph $G$ is

$$
ch_f^s(G)=\inf\{r:G\text{ is }(a,b)\text{-choosable for all integers }a,b\text{ with }a/b\geq r\}.
$$

**Planar graph choosability conjecture.** There exists a constant integer $m$ such that every planar graph is $(5m-1,m)$-choosable.

This conjecture would imply that the strong fractional choice number of the family of planar graphs is strictly less than $5$, improving the known upper bound $ch_f^s(\mathcal{P})\leq 5$.

373173.title: Polynomial-time conjecture for subgraphs with boundedly many components
373173.statement: Let $G$ be a finite graph and let $H$ be a subgraph of $G$ with at most $k$ components, where $k$ is a natural number. The notions **$S$-Eulerian** and **semi $S$-Eulerian** mean, respectively, that $H$ has an $S$-Eulerian circuit or an $S$-Eulerian trail: a closed or open trail in $G$ containing every edge of $H$. **Polynomial-time conjecture.** For every natural number $k$, determining whether $H$ is $S$-Eulerian or semi $S$-Eulerian can be done in polynomial time. The paper establishes NP-completeness for unrestricted subgraphs and a linear-time algorithm for connected subgraphs; the conjecture proposes polynomial-time solvability for every fixed bound on the number of components.

373207.title: The pivot-layer colouring conjecture for diagonal poset Ramsey numbers
373207.statement:
Let $Q_n$ denote the diagonal poset on $n$ elements, and let $R(Q_n,Q_n)$ be its two-colour Ramsey number. For a positive integer $L$, consider the colouring construction in which $2L$ pairs of layers are modified by $2$ families of pivots. **Pivot-layer colouring conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist $L$ and a constant $a$ such that this type of colouring gives

$$
R(Q_n,Q_n)\geq(3-\epsilon)n+a.
$$

The conjecture asserts that optimizing this family of colourings can asymptotically approach a coefficient of $3$, improving on the bounds established in the paper; whether the required choices of layer parameters exist remains open.
373207.review_depth: Source Conjecture 6 and optimization appendix read. Q_n is the Boolean lattice of dimension n, not an n-element antichain. The target quantifies over every epsilon and unbounded L.

373237.title: Böröczky extremality conjecture for monochromatic lines
373237.statement: Let $P$ be a non-collinear set of $n$ two-colored points, and suppose that no line contains more than $(1/2-delta)n$ points, where $delta>0$. **Böröczky extremality conjecture.** For every $delta>0$ there exists $epsilon>0$ such that the number of monochromatic lines determined by $P$ is at least $epsilon n^2$. The Böröczky example has only one monochromatic line when half the points lie on a line, and the conjecture asserts that staying a fixed proportion below this threshold forces quadratically many monochromatic lines.

373328.title: Representability by canonical gain-graph incidence matrices
373328.statement:
Let $(G,\mathcal{B})$ be a biased graph, let $M$ be an elementary lift of the frame matroid $F(G,\mathcal{B})$, and suppose that $M$ is $3$-connected. Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and let $A$ be a matrix representing $M$ over $\mathbb{F}$. **Canonical incidence-matrix conjecture.** There is an $(\mathbb{F}^+\rtimes\mathbb{F}^{\times})$-gain function $\psi$ for $G$ such that

$$
F(G,\mathcal{B})=F(G,\psi/\mathbb{F}^+),
$$

$$
M=M(\mathbb{F}^+\rtimes\mathbb{F}^{\times},\mathbb{F}^+,\mathcal{A},G,\psi),
$$

and $A$ is projectively equivalent to $A(D,\psi)$ for every orientation $D$ of $G$. This asserts that every such representation is, up to projective equivalence, an incidence matrix arising from a gain function.

373328.search_coverage: No exhaustive representability solver completed; finite fields and 3-connectivity must both be certified, and testing only canonical matrices is circular.
373328.remaining_lemmas_or_gaps: Enumerate noncanonical representations of elementary lifts and test projective equivalence, or prove a representation-normalization theorem.

373355.title: Strong light tails conjecture for Erdős sieves
373355.statement: Let $K$ be the number field underlying the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $R$ be an Erdős sieve, and let $B_N$ be the Følner sequence used to define light tails. For a set $A\subset\mathcal{O}_K$, write $-A+R$ for the sieve obtained by adding $-A$ to each level of $R$. **Strong light tails conjecture.** For every Erdős sieve $R$ with strong light tails for $B_N$, there exists some infinite $A\subset\mathcal{O}_K$ such that $-A+R$ has strong light tails for $B_N$. This would rule out, within the class of sieve sets with strong light tails, the positive-density obstruction described by Host, by guaranteeing an infinite additive configuration compatible with the sieve's strong light-tail property.

373367.title: Greedy optimality conjecture for tooth-dominant comb graphs
373367.statement:
Let $C_{n,m}$ be the comb graph with spine parameter $n$ and tooth parameter $m$, let $b(C_{n,m})$ be its burning number, and let $T_{\mathrm{greedy}}^{(S)}$ be the number of fires used by the greedy algorithm when its initial placement is specified by $S$. Define

$$
T_{\mathrm{greedy}}=\min\left\{T_{\mathrm{greedy}}^{(S)}:S=1,2,\ldots,n\right\}.
$$

**Greedy optimality conjecture for comb graphs.** If $n\leq m$, then

$$
b(C_{n,m})=\min\left\{T_{\mathrm{greedy}}^{(S)}:S=1,2,\ldots,n\right\}.
$$

The greedy algorithm is proved optimal in the spine-dominant regime $n\geq m$, while in the tooth-dominant regime it is known to give an approximation and has been confirmed through $m=n+4$. Its optimality for all $n\leq m$ remains open.

373384.title: Goh's Möbius uncertainty conjecture for locally finite posets
373384.statement:
Let $P$ be a locally finite poset, and let $\mu_P(x,y)$ denote its Möbius function. Say that $P$ has the Möbius uncertainty property when this property holds as defined in the paper, and say that $P$ has the Möbius nonvanishing property when, for every $x\in P$, there are infinitely many $y\in P$ such that $\mu_P(x,y)\neq 0$. **Goh's conjecture.** A locally finite poset $P$ has the Möbius uncertainty property if and only if, for every $x\in P$, the set

$$
\{y\in P:\mu_P(x,y)\neq 0\}
$$

is infinite. This conjecture is presented as a special case of Goh's Conjecture 6 and as the assertion that the Möbius uncertainty property is equivalent to the Möbius nonvanishing property; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

373402.title: Conjecture on dyadic congruences for overcolored partition functions
373402.statement:
Let $\bar{a}_{r,s}(n)$ denote the overcolored partition function with parameters $r$ and $s$. For integers $k\geq 1$ and $j,i\geq 0$, consider the parameter pair

$$
r=2^{k+1}j+2^k-1,\qquad s=2^ki+1.
$$

**Dyadic congruence conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 0$, the congruences

$$
\bar{a}_{2^{k+1}j+2^k-1,2^ki+1}(3n+2)\equiv 0 \pmod {2^{k+1}},
$$

$$
\bar{a}_{2^{k+1}j+2^k-1,2^ki+1}(9n+3)\equiv 0 \pmod {2^{k+2}},
$$

$$
\bar{a}_{2^{k+1}j+2^k-1,2^ki+1}(9n+6)\equiv 0 \pmod {2^{k+2}}.
$$

These congruences extend the paper's arithmetic investigations of the overcolored partition function; the concluding remark specifically calls for an elementary proof of the congruences in this conjecture, and no resolution is supplied in the given text.

373403.title: Type B real-rootedness conjecture for the polynomials $B_n$
373403.statement: Let $B_n$ be the type B polynomials defined in the paper, for $n\geq 1$. A polynomial is **real-rooted** if all of its roots are real. **Type B real-rootedness conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$, the polynomials $B_n$ are real-rooted. The preceding corollary establishes that the polynomials $B_n$ are $\gamma$-positive, and real-rootedness would further imply $\gamma$-positivity and ultra log-concavity for palindromic polynomials with nonnegative coefficients; the source gives no resolution status for this type B analogue.

373442.title: Length-profile bounds and parity conjectures for hypercube drawings
373442.statement: Consider a length-regular drawing of the $d$-dimensional hypercube, with edge lengths $\ell_1\leq \ell_2\leq\cdots$. **Length-profile conjectures.** The following assertions are proposed: (1) for every $i$, $\ell_i\leq 2^{d-1}-2^{d-(i+1)}$; (2) there must exist edges of even length, with the dimension qualification left unresolved in the source; and (3) if a length $\ell$ is odd, it cannot occur twice, with the source suggesting a qualification of $d\geq 3$ or $d\geq 4$. These claims concern structural restrictions on length-regular hypercube drawings. The tentative dimension qualifications and the informal presentation make the precise scope unclear, and the source gives no resolution.

373462.title: Apex extension conjecture for degree Turán densities
373462.statement:
Let $F$ be a $(k-1)$-graph, and let $\mathcal{S}_F$ be the $k$-graph obtained by adjoining an apex vertex $v$ and including $v\cup e$ as an edge for every $e\in E(F)$. For $2\leq\ell<k$, one always has $\pi_\ell(\mathcal{S}_F)\leq\pi_{\ell-1}(F)$. **Apex extension conjecture.** For integers $3\leq\ell<k$,

$$
\pi_\ell(\mathcal{S}_F)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\pi_{\ell-1}(F)=0.
$$

The forward implication is known for $\ell=2$ via the paper's $2$-vanishing-order theorem, while the analogous equivalence for $\ell\geq3$ is proposed as an open direction.

373482.title: Rank-5 toy Rota Basis Conjecture for circuit-rich pools

This is a finite, experiment-specific claim about the stated generated class; it is not the general Rota Basis Conjecture and is not established beyond the reported computational setting.

373514.title: Geelen's simulation conjecture for vertex-minor-closed graph classes
373514.statement: A graph class is **vertex-minor-closed** if it contains every vertex-minor of each of its graphs. **Geelen's simulation conjecture.** Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is efficiently classically simulable on every vertex-minor-closed class of graphs other than the class of all graphs. The conjecture is known for circle graphs and for graphs of bounded rank-width, but remains open for arbitrary vertex-minor-closed classes.

373545.title: Pairwise negative correlation conjecture for random-cluster measures
373545.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, and let $\phi_{p,q}=\phi_{p,q}(G)$ be the random-cluster measure on $G$ with parameter $q\in(0,1)$. A probability measure on $\{0,1\}^E$ satisfies **pairwise negative correlation** (p-NC) if, for all distinct edges $e,f\in E$, 

$$
\mu\big[\omega(e)=\omega(f)=1\big]\leqslant \mu\big[\omega(e)=1\big]\mu\big[\omega(f)=1\big].
$$

**Random-cluster p-NC conjecture.** The measures $\phi_{p,q}$ satisfy the p-NC property.

For $q\in(0,1)$, these measures satisfy the negative lattice condition, but that condition is neither necessary nor sufficient for p-NC. The conjecture proposes a weak form of negative dependence for random-cluster measures in the subunit-$q$ regime.

373546.title: Pairwise negative correlation conjecture for the uniform forest measure
373546.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph, and let $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{UF}}$ denote the uniform forest measure on $G$. A probability measure on $\{0,1\}^E$ satisfies **pairwise negative correlation** (p-NC) if, for all distinct edges $e,f\in E$, 

$$
\mu\big[\omega(e)=\omega(f)=1\big]\leqslant \mu\big[\omega(e)=1\big]\mu\big[\omega(f)=1\big].
$$

**Uniform forest p-NC conjecture.** The measure $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{UF}}$ satisfies the p-NC property.

This is presented as a special case of the random-cluster p-NC conjecture and of the conjectured p-NC property for the arboreal gas model. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

373561.title: The spectral diffusion conjecture for Collatz orbit measures
373561.statement:
Let $\mu_K$ be the orbit measure on $\mathbb{Z}/2^K\mathbb{Z}$, let $\operatorname{hw}(\xi)$ denote Hamming weight, and define the spectral content at weight $w$ by

$$
\mathcal{S}_w(K)=\frac{1}{\binom Kw}\sum_{\operatorname{hw}(\xi)=w}|\widehat{\mu}_K(\xi)|^2.
$$
 **Spectral diffusion conjecture.** For every convergent Collatz orbit with odd-step density $\rho<1/\log_2 3$, there is $C(\rho)>0$ such that, for every $w\ge1$,

$$
\mathcal{S}_w(K)\le C(\rho)2^{-\alpha_w K},
$$
 where $\alpha_w>0$ depends only on $w$. The conjecture formalizes decay of Walsh spectral content with modular depth; the supplied text gives supporting numerical observations but no proof.
